tldr: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, reported as having occurred rather than as a forecast.
title: 2026 edition REPORT
insights: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year while sessions rose 21%.

Globally, gaming app install and session growth varied by subvertical year over year from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy installs declined 1% while sessions grew 57%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Globally, all-games gaming app retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025: day 1 retention was 27% and day 30 retention was 5%. Global gaming app CPI rose to $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI declined from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while deal discovery CPI increased from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

commentary: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025. In 2025, consumer spending in the mobile-app market rose 10.6% year over year to $167 billion. In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%. Globally, gaming app growth from 2024 to 2025 varied by subvertical: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%. The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data.

editorial_plan.report_thesis: The benchmark shows that app acquisition and engagement patterns vary by vertical and region, supporting a category-specific reading of performance alongside the report’s recommendation for integrated measurement to inform optimization and budget allocation.

themes.theme: Market scale and outlook: the report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

summary.tldr: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, reported as having occurred rather than as a forecast.
summary.card_tldr_compact: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
summary.executive_summary: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025. In 2025, consumer spending in the mobile-app market rose 10.6% year over year to $167 billion. In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%. Globally, gaming app growth from 2024 to 2025 varied by subvertical: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%. The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data.

verified_fact.statement: For finance apps, global session length increased 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. In 2025, North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, and LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes. Session length declined from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

artifacts.expert_comment: In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%. Global e-commerce app CPI declined from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while deal discovery CPI increased from $1.44 to $2.26. The implication is that acquisition alone and the all-e-commerce CPI measure each give an incomplete view: session direction diverged from installs in e-commerce and finance, while deal discovery CPI moved opposite to the all-e-commerce figure. For budget reviews, MarketLense would pair category-level install, session, and CPI views with integrated measurement rather than rely on any one signal.
artifacts.linkedin_post:
Global finance app installs fell 4% year over year in 2025, while sessions rose 21%. Acquisition and usage moved in opposite directions.

That distinction matters when describing performance: install volume alone does not capture the reported session trend.

MarketLense’s recommendation: when assessing finance-app performance, keep installs and sessions as separate measures.

verified_facts.statement: For finance apps, global session length increased 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. In 2025, North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, and LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes. Session length declined from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

claim_ledgers.claim_text: The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
In 2025, consumer spending in the mobile-app market rose 10.6% year over year to $167 billion.
In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Globally, gaming app growth from 2024 to 2025 varied by subvertical: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data.

The report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
In 2025, global e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%; global finance app installs fell 4% year over year while sessions rose 21%.

Globally, gaming app install and session growth varied by subvertical year over year from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy installs declined 1% while sessions grew 57%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Globally, all-games gaming app retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025: day 1 retention was 27% and day 30 retention was 5%. Global gaming app CPI rose to $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI declined from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while deal discovery CPI increased from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: in 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, while LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes and session length declined in APAC from 7.07 to 6.94 minutes, Europe from 5.77 to 5.62 minutes, and MENA from 6.61 to 6.39 minutes.

The report recommends an integrated, adaptable, and accountable data foundation for app marketers, combining cross-channel attribution to remove blind spots and expose trends, AI insights for faster and more effective analysis, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and confident budget allocation based on aggregated data. This is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

findings.text: For finance apps, global session length increased 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. planned_themes: Market scale and outlook: the report records more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025 and mobile-app-market consumer spending up 10.6% year over year to $167 billion; separately, mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

Global 2025 acquisition and usage diverged in both categories: e-commerce app installs fell 10% year over year while sessions rose 5%, and finance app installs fell 4% while sessions rose 21%.

Global gaming growth varied by subvertical from 2024 to 2025: Casual installs grew 19% and sessions 37%; Strategy sessions grew 57% while installs declined 1%; Casino installs grew 22% while sessions declined 5%; and Slots installs grew 46% while sessions declined 5%.
Global all-games gaming retention showed minimal change from 2024 to 2025, with day 1 retention at 27% and day 30 at 5%; separately, overall global gaming app CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Global e-commerce app CPI moved down from $1.00 in 2024 to $0.98 in 2025, while CPI for the deal discovery category rose from $1.44 to $2.26 over the same period.

Finance indicators varied by region and measure: for 2024–2025, LATAM finance-app installs grew 76% and sessions 57%; finance-app session length increased globally 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025, with North America highest among regions at 8.43 minutes, LATAM rising to 5.87 minutes, and declines from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

The report recommends that app marketers use an integrated, adaptable, accountable data foundation combining cross-channel attribution, AI insights, and next-generation solutions for campaign optimization and budget allocation based on aggregated data; this is a recommendation, not a measured outcome.

doc_map.title: Mobile app trends: 2026 edition
doc_map.summary: A global benchmark of mobile app performance, combining industry context and 2026 marketing themes with performance analyses of gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps. The report uses aggregated, anonymized data from apps tracked by Adjust from January 2024 to January 2026, alongside some third-party industry estimates.

sections.title: Introduction: Evolution and opportunity in the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Introduces the growth outlook for mobile apps and the measurement and marketing challenges created by fragmented channels, evolving user behavior, and AI. It frames the report as a benchmark for gaming, e-commerce, and finance.
key_points: The report cites more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, an estimated 5.8 billion unique smartphone users, and consumer spending of $167 billion, up 10.6% year over year.
It describes experimentation with AI, automation, and channel diversification as key features of 2025, while emphasizing the need for actionable data and cross-channel attribution.

In the chart “App install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs rose 10% and sessions 7% in 2025, compared with growth of 8% and 2%, respectively, in 2024; February 2025 installs were 13% below the yearly average, while December installs were 8% above it.
For Q1 2025 versus Q1 2026 global ATT opt-in rates, the industry average rose from 35% to 38%; gaming reached 39%, while e-commerce/shopping declined from 35% to 34%.

sections.title: AI transforms from strategic tool to core infrastructure in 2026
sections.summary: Describes AI being integrated into marketing and measurement workflows through data-analysis assistants, predictive audience segmentation, and practical generative-AI use. It notes that organizational maturity remains uneven.
key_points: AI assistants can query multi-channel data in natural language and surface analysis, reports, and visualizations in real time.
Audience segments are shifting from manually maintained static lists to dynamic groups based on behavior, intent, and likelihood to convert.

Generative AI is being used to test creative variants, model user journeys, and tailor in-app messaging; most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while a small advanced group reportedly achieved efficiency gains above 20%.

sections.title: Mobile-first approach evolves into multi-platform strategy
sections.summary: Argues that customer journeys now move across mobile web, desktop, apps, and other channels, making cross-platform measurement and deep linking important for attribution and conversion.
key_points: Only around 31% of marketers report complete satisfaction with their ability to unify and read data across platforms.
Cross-platform measurement connects activity such as a mobile-web session to an in-app conversion, revealing channel contributions beyond last-click credit.
The report recommends integrated measurement, high-quality deep linking, user segmentation, retargeting, and web-to-app solutions to reduce journey barriers.

sections.title: Key takeaways & methodology
sections.summary: Summarizes selected year-over-year findings across the three app verticals and explains the report’s dataset, coverage, regions, and date range.
key_points: The takeaways report global e-commerce app sessions increased 5%; LATAM finance installs and sessions rose 76% and 57%; and gaming retention remained flat, with day 1 at 27% and day 30 at 5%.
The methodology covers e-commerce/shopping, finance/fintech, and gaming across global, APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America.
The dataset combines Adjust’s top 5,000 apps with the total set of apps tracked by Adjust, with data sources covering 45 countries and approximately 250 countries under the ISO 3166-1 standard.
The stated date range is January 2024–January 2026; the report says figures are aggregated and anonymized and may not represent the entire global app market.

sections.title: Gaming apps
sections.summary: Opens the report’s first vertical chapter, introducing the gaming-app benchmark before the dedicated “Finding and keeping users” analysis begins on page 17.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Analyzes gaming acquisition, sessions, retention, install costs, and partner networks across regions and subverticals for 2024–2025. The results show growth and retention patterns diverging by game type.
key_points: In “Gaming app install and session growth percentages YoY 2024 - 2025 (Global),” casual games grew 19% in installs and 37% in sessions; hyper casual grew 4% and 31%; strategy sessions rose 57% despite flat installs; casino and slots installs grew 22% and 46%, while sessions fell 5% in each.

For “Gaming app retention rates 2024 - 2025 (Global),” all games remained at 27% day 1, 13% day 7, 8% day 14, and 5% day 30 retention; hyper casual retention was 27%, 8%, 6%, and 2% at those same days in 2025. Global gaming CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Regional install/session growth was mixed: MENA recorded +2%/+7%, Europe -7%/+3%, LATAM -9%/+0.4%, and North America -5%/-2% in 2025.
Gaming partners per app averaged 5.3 in 2025, down from 6 in 2024; hybrid casual, idle RPG, and simulation moved against that decline, increasing to 9.8, 6.7, and 6.8 partners, respectively.

sections.title: E-commerce/shopping apps
sections.summary: Opens the second vertical chapter, which proceeds to analyze e-commerce and shopping user acquisition, engagement, retention, and costs. The dedicated “Finding and keeping users” section begins on page 27.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Compares e-commerce growth and acquisition patterns across regions and subverticals, then examines retention, CPI, paid/organic mix, and partner counts. Overall sessions increased even as total installs declined.
key_points: In “E-commerce app install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs fell 10% year over year in 2025 while sessions rose 5%; LATAM led regional growth with installs up 17% and sessions up 30%.

For “E-commerce app retention rates 2024 - 2025 (Global),” day 1 retention declined from 13.2% to 12.6%, day 7 from 6.3% to 6%, and day 30 stayed at 3%. In “E-commerce app CPI 2024 - 2025 (Global),” overall CPI fell from $1 to $0.98, while deal discovery CPI rose from $1.44 to $2.26.

The global e-commerce paid/organic ratio increased from 0.48 in 2024 to 0.54 in 2025; MENA rose from 0.54 to 0.63, APAC from 0.43 to 0.49, and North America from 0.38 to 0.42, while LATAM and Europe declined.
E-commerce partners per app averaged 6.3 in 2025; deal discovery and marketplace/classifieds increased to 9 and 10, while shopping decreased to 6.

sections.title: Finance apps
sections.summary: Opens the third vertical chapter, followed by analysis of finance-app acquisition, engagement, costs, and channel mix. The dedicated “Finding and keeping users” section begins on page 34.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Examines finance-app installs and sessions, regional variation, retention, session length, CPI, paid/organic acquisition, and partner counts. Session activity rose substantially even as installs declined globally.
key_points: In “Finance app install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs fell 4% year over year in 2025 while sessions rose 21%; February installs were 14% below the yearly average and December installs were 8% above it.
For “Finance app install and session growth percentages YoY 2024 - 2025,” LATAM recorded +76% installs and +57% sessions; APAC recorded +5% and +50%; Europe +15% and +19%; and MENA +42% and +10%.

Global finance app session length rose 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025; North America led at 8.43 minutes, while session length declined in APAC, Europe, and MENA. Day 0 sessions per user globally fell from 1.52 to 1.48.
Finance CPI fell globally from $1.51 in 2024 to $1.13 in 2025, while the global paid/organic ratio rose to 1.13; LATAM’s ratio increased to 3.26.

sections.title: Conclusion: An exciting future for the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Concludes that app growth depends on understanding whole, cross-device journeys and integrating attribution, AI insights, and optimization capabilities. The contents page lists the conclusion at page 41, while the displayed conclusion page is labeled 40.
key_points: The report characterizes finance apps as increasingly embedded in daily life, e-commerce as accelerating through AI personalization and agents, and gaming as balancing user acquisition with retention and sustained engagement.
It recommends integrated, adaptable, and accountable measurement and optimization foundations to reduce blind spots and support budget allocation based on aggregated data.

sections.title: About Adjust
sections.summary: Provides a short description of Adjust’s app measurement and analytics business and states the report’s data basis, variability caveat, and disclaimer. No printed page label is visible in the provided excerpt.
key_points: The report states that its data is aggregated and anonymized and comes from apps tracked by Adjust between January 2024 and January 2026.
It cautions that results may vary by vertical, region, and business model, and that forecasts based on third-party industry estimates are subject to change.

scope.scope: A global benchmark of mobile app performance, covering overall industry trends and gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps, with regional analysis including APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America. Performance trends are reported for January 2024–December 2025, including year-over-year comparisons for 2024 and 2025.

methods: Uses Adjust data to report app installs and sessions globally, with monthly trends from January 2024 to December 2025 and year-over-year comparisons for 2024–2025. The excerpts do not specify the app sample frame or a validation method.

findings.text: Globally in 2025, casual games grew 19% in installs and 37% in sessions; hyper casual grew 4% in installs and 31% in sessions; strategy sessions grew 57% despite flat installs; and casino and slots installs grew 22% and 46%, respectively, while sessions decreased 5% in each.
findings.evidence: Installs of casual games grew 19% YoY in 2025, alongside a boost of 37% in sessions. As we explored above, despite being an install-led category, hyper casual’s sessions increased 31%—much higher than their 4% install increase. Strategy games led session growth at +57% despite flat install growth, demonstrating the large number of loyal users the genre has. Casino and slots both achieved strong install growth of 22% and 46%, but sessions decreased 5% in each category, meaning churn may need to be addressed. limitations: The report says GenAI maturity varies: most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while efficiency gains over 20% are reported only for a small group with advanced deployment.
The report describes finance apps’ shift toward paid acquisition as likely linked to falling costs, rather than establishing the cause.
For some gaming categories, sessions fell despite install growth; the report says churn may need to be addressed.

quote_candidates.text: In 2026, sustainable app growth will depend on capturing user journeys across web, app, and other connected environments. It’s no longer sufficient to view users in device silos when we know that conversion is influenced by multiple touchpoints.
With user acquisition costs at a premium, the focus has moved from adding partners to identifying which channels deliver users with the highest proven or predicted lifetime value (pLTV).
Data is still the foundation, but the bar for quality has been raised.
In 2026, the playbook of chasing one channel at a time or pursuing isolated metrics doesn't work anymore.
The next phase of growth is architectural, not because of any single tool, but because of how these capabilities work together.

Teams that build this kind of foundation—integrated, adaptable, and accountable—will be best positioned to navigate the complexity of 2026 and help define what success looks like in a multi-platform world.

report_context.title: 2026 edition REPORT
report_context.overview: Mobile app trends: 2026 edition A global benchmark of mobile app performance, combining industry context and 2026 marketing themes with performance analyses of gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps. The report uses aggregated, anonymized data from apps tracked by Adjust from January 2024 to January 2026, alongside some third-party industry estimates. A global benchmark of mobile app performance, covering overall industry trends and gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps, with regional analysis including APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America. Performance trends are reported for January 2024–December 2025, including year-over-year comparisons for 2024 and 2025.
methods: Uses Adjust data to report app installs and sessions globally, with monthly trends from January 2024 to December 2025 and year-over-year comparisons for 2024–2025. The excerpts do not specify the app sample frame or a validation method.
key_findings: There were more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
Global consumer spending on apps rose to $167 billion in 2025.
Mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Eight of the top 10 mobile games in 2025 each generated more than $1 billion in player spending.
The global mobile-gamer population reached nearly 3 billion in 2025, representing more than 80% of the global gaming population.
Gaming app installs in MENA grew 2% year over year in 2025.
limitations: The report says GenAI maturity varies: most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while efficiency gains over 20% are reported only for a small group with advanced deployment.
The report describes finance apps’ shift toward paid acquisition as likely linked to falling costs, rather than establishing the cause.
For some gaming categories, sessions fell despite install growth; the report says churn may need to be addressed.

sections.section_label: Introduction: Evolution and opportunity in the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Introduces the growth outlook for mobile apps and the measurement and marketing challenges created by fragmented channels, evolving user behavior, and AI. It frames the report as a benchmark for gaming, e-commerce, and finance.
key_points: The report cites more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, an estimated 5.8 billion unique smartphone users, and consumer spending of $167 billion, up 10.6% year over year.
It describes experimentation with AI, automation, and channel diversification as key features of 2025, while emphasizing the need for actionable data and cross-channel attribution.

sections.section_label: AI transforms from strategic tool to core infrastructure in 2026
sections.summary: Describes AI being integrated into marketing and measurement workflows through data-analysis assistants, predictive audience segmentation, and practical generative-AI use. It notes that organizational maturity remains uneven.
key_points: AI assistants can query multi-channel data in natural language and surface analysis, reports, and visualizations in real time.
Audience segments are shifting from manually maintained static lists to dynamic groups based on behavior, intent, and likelihood to convert.
Generative AI is being used to test creative variants, model user journeys, and tailor in-app messaging; most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while a small advanced group reportedly...

sections.section_label: Mobile-first approach evolves into multi-platform strategy
sections.summary: Argues that customer journeys now move across mobile web, desktop, apps, and other channels, making cross-platform measurement and deep linking important for attribution and conversion.
key_points: Only around 31% of marketers report complete satisfaction with their ability to unify and read data across platforms.
Cross-platform measurement connects activity such as a mobile-web session to an in-app conversion, revealing channel contributions beyond last-click credit.
The report recommends integrated measurement, high-quality deep linking, user segmentation, retargeting, and web-to-app solutions to reduce journey barriers.

sections.summary: Summarizes selected year-over-year findings across the three app verticals and explains the report’s dataset, coverage, regions, and date range.
key_points: The takeaways report global e-commerce app sessions increased 5%; LATAM finance installs and sessions rose 76% and 57%; and gaming retention remained flat, with day 1 at 27% and day 30 at 5%.
The methodology covers e-commerce/shopping, finance/fintech, and gaming across global, APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America.
The dataset combines Adjust’s top 5,000 apps with the total set of apps tracked by Adjust, with data sources covering 45 countries and approximately 250 countries under the ISO 3166-1 standard.

sections.summary: Opens the report’s first vertical chapter, introducing the gaming-app benchmark before the dedicated “Finding and keeping users” analysis begins on page 17.

Analyzes gaming acquisition, sessions, retention, install costs, and partner networks across regions and subverticals for 2024–2025. The results show growth and retention patterns diverging by game type.

For “Gaming app retention rates 2024 - 2025 (Global),” all games remained at 27% day 1, 13% day 7, 8% day 14, and 5% day 30 retention; hyper casual retention was 27%, 8%, 6%, and 2% at those same d...
Regional install/session growth was mixed: MENA recorded +2%/+7%, Europe -7%/+3%, LATAM -9%/+0.4%, and North America -5%/-2% in 2025.

findings.text: For finance apps, global session length increased 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025. In 2025, North America had the highest regional session length at 8.43 minutes, and LATAM rose to 5.87 minutes. Session length declined from 2024 to 2025 in APAC (7.07 to 6.94 minutes), Europe (5.77 to 5.62 minutes), and MENA (6.61 to 6.39 minutes).

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The finance-app percentage changes lack an explicit comparison period, unlike the e-commerce changes. The bound source identifies the finance values as year-over-year changes.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The text asserts 2025 consumer spending rose 10.6% to $167 billion, but this item is bound only to the app-downloads fact. That binding does not support the spending metric or values; the separate spending fact cannot be borrowed for this item.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app declines and increases lack an explicit comparison period. [public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app declines and increases lack an explicit comparison period. The bound fact specifies year-over-year changes for finance installs and sessions too; the reader should not have to infer that comparator from the preceding clause.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The e-commerce changes are explicitly year over year, but the finance-app changes have no explicit comparison period. The bound fact specifies a year-over-year comparison for the finance figures as well.

[public_editorial_quality.report_limitations_omitted] The report covers the planned findings, but it presents several benchmark rates and retention/session measures without disclosing material source limitations: the verified facts state that sample sizes and/or underlying denominators are not provided. That caveat matters when readers interpret or compare the results, and no public item makes it clear. Dimensions: limitations: The source fact map records missing sample sizes and/or underlying denominators for multiple benchmark measures, but the public report does not disclose this methodological limitation for readers evaluating or comparing those measures.
